genre_name: Cis-Mendelian randomisation plus colocalisation of a protein or drug target
scope: Drug-target / cis-MR papers that proxy perturbation of a protein or drug target with variants in or near its encoding gene (cis-pQTLs, cis-eQTLs, or gene-region variants associated with a downstream biomarker) and test the effect on disease outcomes, backed by Bayesian colocalisation (coloc, coloc-SuSiE, eCAVIAR, HyPrColoc), with optional positive controls, phenome-wide safety scans, directionality tests and replication. Covers single/multi-target papers and proteome-wide drug-target MR + coloc screens. Excludes genome-wide polygenic two-sample MR of lifestyle exposures, transcriptome-wide single-cell MR, GWAS discovery papers whose MR is secondary, MR methods papers and reviews.
word_count_convention: jats_structure.py prose words; captions/tables/citations/headings excluded; main = I+M+R+D(+L,C); statement subsections inside Methods (data availability, ethics, role of funders, reporting-summary boilerplate) removed

checklists.name: coloc method and priors (Giambartolomei 2014)
checklists.citation: Giambartolomei C, Vukcevic D, Schadt EE, et al. Bayesian test for colocalisation between pairs of genetic association studies using summary statistics. PLoS Genet. 2014;10(5):e1004383
checklists.frequency: 5/8 cite it (E2, E3, E5, E7, E8); E4 cites coloc/coloc-SuSiE (Wallace); 5/8 state priors, all with p12 = 1e-5 where stated
checklists.notes: Assumes at most one causal variant per trait in the region (coloc-SuSiE relaxes this; used only by E4). Wallace 2020 (PLoS Genet 16:e1008720, not re-read here) argues the default p12 = 1e-5 is permissive and recommends a prior-sensitivity check; none of the exemplars shows one.

limitations.placement: unheaded paragraph(s) near the end of the Discussion (5/8); Discussion subsection with heading (2/8: Cell Press 'Limitations of the study', 'Caveats and limitations'); separate top-level 'Limitations' (1/8, JAMA author manuscript)
conventions: preceded by a strengths paragraph (5/8: E1, E2, E4, E5, E7)
opens with a signal sentence ('This work has several limitations')
enumerated with ordinal words First ... Last (5/8: E1, E3, E4, E5, E7)
most limitations are followed by a mitigation (sensitivity analysis, replication, prior evidence)
followed by an 'In summary/In conclusion' paragraph or a Conclusions heading

standard_items.text: Genetic proxies reflect small, lifelong perturbation of the target; a drug acts later, for a shorter time and at larger magnitude, so MR informs direction and on-target effects, not the drug's effect size or timing
Samples were mostly or only European (or mixed-ancestry data were combined), limiting transportability to other ancestries
Few cis instruments and limited cases for some outcomes or subtypes reduce power; nulls are not evidence of no effect
Exclusion restriction cannot be fully verified; residual horizontal pleiotropy is possible even with cis instruments and more likely with trans-pQTLs
Colocalisation assumes one causal variant per trait, has limited power (low PP.H4 is not evidence against sharing) and cannot separate neighbouring genes in LD
Protein levels from affinity assays may reflect epitope/aptamer-binding effects, differ between platforms (SomaScan vs Olink) and were measured once
Outcome definitions and recruitment differ across consortia/biobanks; subtype misclassification possible
MR is indirect evidence; functional studies or trials are needed before clinical use
Selection into biobanks (e.g. UK Biobank) or conditioning on diagnosis can induce collider bias
Circulating protein or eQTL levels may not reflect the target tissue (brain, aorta)
Overlap between exposure and outcome samples can bias estimates towards the confounded association when instruments are weak
Estimates assume linearity, no gene-environment or gene-gene interaction, and proportional scaling across targets

variation_notes: Two sub-designs share one skeleton. Single/multi-target papers (E1, E2, E3, E5; E8 narrows a scan to one target) weight cis variants by a downstream biomarker (SBP, citrate, HDL-C, HbA1c) or by a cis-pQTL/eQTL, report a handful of outcomes, often a PheWAS-style safety scan, and compare with trial evidence; their displays are forest plots, regional plots and instrument tables. Proteome-wide papers (E4, E6, E7) test 1,000-3,000 proteins from deCODE/UKB-PPP/Fenland, split cis vs trans instruments, apply Bonferroni/FDR, tier hits by MR + coloc + SMR/HEIDI + replication, and add enrichment/druggability; their displays are a workflow figure, a volcano/Manhattan plot, a heatmap and a tiered summary table. Venue house style drives the rest: Methods last in Nature Communications and Cell Press (STAR Methods with key resources table and a mandatory 'Limitations of the study'); JAMA moves Methods to eMethods (355 words) and adds Key Points; PLOS Medicine adds an Author summary and attaches the STROBE-MR checklist; Lancet family adds Research in context and a Funding line in the abstract; AHA adds Clinical Perspective and an unheaded Introduction. Only the PLOS, BMC and Lancet-family exemplars cite STROBE-MR; none states pre-registration; code availability is weak (4/8).
lint_notes: Title and abstract must name Mendelian randomization (8/8; STROBE-MR item 1) and the target/protein; proteome-wide papers say 'proteome-wide'.

Methods must contain, in any order: exposure QTL/biomarker source with N and ancestry; cis window around the encoding gene; P threshold; clumping r2 + LD reference (or LD-aware IVW); F-statistics; primary estimator; sensitivity estimators; coloc method, priors (p1, p2, p12) and PP.H4 threshold; multiple-testing rule. Flag any missing item.

Every MR-significant target-outcome pair must have a colocalisation result (PP.H4, ideally also PP.H3) reported in text, figure or table; a regional plot for each colocalised locus belongs in main or supplement.

MR estimates must be shown as a forest plot or a results table with OR/beta, 95% CI and P, scaled to a stated unit (per SD of protein, per 10 mmHg SBP, per SD HbA1c lowering) and signed as target inhibition vs higher level.
Per-variant instrument table (SNP, EA, EAF, beta, SE, P, F) must exist in main or supplement (STROBE-MR items 10-11); 6/8 exemplars have one.
Proteome-wide drafts must report the number of proteins tested, the Bonferroni/FDR family and threshold, separate cis from trans results, and show a volcano/Manhattan-style screen plot.
Limitations must include the genetic-vs-pharmacological caveat and the ancestry caveat; proteome drafts must add the assay/epitope caveat; coloc drafts the single-causal-variant caveat.

Data availability must name each GWAS/pQTL source with an accession or URL (IEU OpenGWAS ID, GCST, FinnGen release); code availability should give a repository (genre median is weak; do not copy the genre's omission).
Ethics statement is one or two sentences: original studies' approvals and consent; no new approval for summary statistics.
Attach a completed STROBE-MR checklist even though only 2/8 exemplars do; PLOS ONE requires it and adds a second-independent-dataset requirement (replication present in 6/8).
Directionality (Steiger or reverse MR) is optional in this genre (3/8); do not fail drafts that omit it when instruments are cis-acting, but require it for trans instruments.
MR scatter/leave-one-out plots are rare (2/8, supplement) because cis instruments are few; require them only when a target has more than 2 instruments.
Word ranges: main text 3,350-6,050 (median about 4,150); excluding Methods 2,350-3,950; abstract 150-450 (median about 300); references 50-86.
notes: Exemplar mix: PLOS (E1), BMC (E2), Nature (E3), Cell Press (E4), Lancet family/Elsevier (E5), JAMA (E6), AHA (E7), ERS (E8). Single/multi-target 5, proteome-wide 3.

E6 is the Europe PMC author manuscript (CC BY 4.0), not the typeset JAMA article: Methods and statements may be shorter than the published version; its data sharing statement and author contributions could not be verified.

E5 uses colocalisation only to select instruments (eQTL vs HbA1c, probability > 0.7) and E3 uses it to check the cross-ancestry instrument signal; exposure-outcome colocalisation is present in the other 6/8.

Supplement contents for E5, E6 and E8 were inferred from in-text references to supplementary tables/figures; the files themselves were not opened. E3's file list came from its 'Description of Additional Supplementary Files'.
No exemplar shows a PheWAS figure or a prior-sensitivity plot for coloc; both are listed as Amani options rather than genre requirements.

Body-text contamination audit: title/abstract/keywords are clean for all 8. E6 mentions a joint disease once in its Discussion (IL-23 context); no exemplar uses a joint, motor-neuron or pancreatic outcome.

Candidates rejected: Cell Genomics 2022 multi-ancestry proteome MR (joint-disease outcomes), Nat Commun 2022 stroke proteome MR (joint-disease PheWAS rows), JAHA 2025 IL-6/small-vessel disease and JAMA Netw Open 2023 thiazide/kidney stones (no colocalisation), Diabetes Care 2026 GLP1R (no colocalisation).
